infinite hill for schools

infinite hill for schools is planned — it launches after the pilot, and no school is using it yet. here's the plan: the kid will never pay, the teacher will try it free, and the school will pay less than the textbook it replaces.

how it will work

a classroom code, a hill, a certificate.

join in ten seconds
the teacher will share a classroom code. students will join with it. no accounts to set up, nothing to install.
assign a camp, a week, a session
the class will climb together. the hill on the classroom screen at the start of the period will show who walked yesterday.
see who’s stuck
a progress view: who walked, who’s stuck, what they kept. nothing to grade by hand.
a certificate at every lookout
printable, with the door’s seal. parents will see the strand at home.
two products in one house

your own door, or all eight.

for faith schools
teach your own door, devotionally — a Catholic school will run the Catholic door, a Jewish day school the Jewish door. every session will be written from your tradition’s texts and read by a scholar of your tradition. nothing blended. nothing compared. kids will climb for credit.
for every other school
religious literacy, taught properly: eight doors, each by its own people. students will learn about every tradition and practice none in class. we never write a prayer and never say which door is true — which is what makes the house usable in a public school.
what teachers will get

a classroom code students join in ten seconds · assign a camp, a week, or a single session · a progress view · the hill on the classroom screen · a printable certificate at each lookout · a scholar of your tradition you can call · nothing to grade by hand.

how it will be priced
one classroom
free
for a term. that’s how a teacher will find out.
the school
per student, per year
a fraction of the textbook. dashboard, assignments, certificates, reporting, a scholar to call. districts and dioceses: volume pricing and single sign-on.
what we will promise schools
built for under-13s
no ads, no trackers, no selling data, and a student-privacy policy a district can sign.
every line checked
a scholar of your tradition will read it before a child hears it. you'll be able to call them.
